title: OpenFIR v2.0: Standards-Aligned Hybrid TLS 1.3 and UDP GSO/GRO File & Directory Transfer Protocol with Zero-Dependency All-Platform Native Frosted-Glass GUIs and Linux TUI
description: Defensive publication and clean-room Apache-2.0 reference implementation of OpenFIR (Open Fast Interleaved Reliable Transport Protocol) v2.0, uniting the high-BDP hybrid transport core with a zero-third-party-dependency native GUI and Linux TUI client suite across six platforms (Linux C11 TrueColor TUI, Linux C++20 X11/Xft Gaussian-Blur GUI, Windows C++20 Direct2D/DWM Acrylic GUI, macOS Swift AppKit Vibrancy GUI, iOS 15+ SwiftUI Material GUI, and Android 8-15+ pure-SDK Kotlin/RenderEffect GUI) bound via an in-process C ABI (include/openfir.h). Core transport mechanisms include: (1) Single-port dual-stack hybrid transport combining RFC 8446 TLS 1.3 (ALPN openfir/1) control and parallel TCP data lanes with an open 17-byte AAD UDP data lane (OF1\x01) protected by RFC 5705 ExportKeyingMaterial channel-bound mutual authentication, Argon2id KDF, ephemeral X25519 PFS AES-256-GCM, and a 16,384-packet sliding anti-replay window; (2) Sub-second hybrid UDP/TLS-1.3 failover defending against ISP UDP QoS policing and mid-stream UDP blackholes, accelerated on Linux via UDP_SEGMENT (GSO), UDP_GRO ancillary cmsg unbatching, and SO_REUSEPORT; (3) Zero-cold-start content-defined chunking based on classic 1981 Rabin polynomial rolling fingerprints over GF(2)[x] paired with exact 0%-false-positive interactive TLS CAS negotiation and streaming BLAKE2b-256 binary Merkle tree end-to-end verification; (4) Clean-room systematic Cauchy GF(256) Reed-Solomon adaptive forward error correction enforcing strictly 0% parity overhead on lossless links while recovering contiguous multi-packet burst drops; (5) Dimensionless normalized Kalman one-way delay-gradient and delivery-rate congestion control with RFC 6298 dynamic RTT-scaled retransmission cooldowns and CAR-safe burst pacing; and (6) Bidirectional push/pull transfers, tarless O(log N) VirtualDirectoryExtent streaming, and persistent crash-resumable staging journals (.openfir-part and .openfir-state).
